newsitem.title: UK: Weak sterling pushes LIFFE grain futures up.
newsitem.headline: Weak sterling pushes LIFFE grain futures up.

text.p: LIFFE wheat and barley prices rose as sterling eased against continental currencies.
"We're looking at sterling. It's the lowest it's been for ages," one trader, who was referring to the UK unit's performance against the German mark, said.
There had been some merchant interest, and volume was reasonable, he said.
But the focus had been on the nearby, with new crop positions largely neglected.
Of a total volume of 484 lots of wheat, 107 were on March and 343 on May, the active month.
They also had the biggest rises. March and May both rose by 1.50 stg per tonne, with March last traded at 94.50 stg and May last traded at 96.50.
Barley also rose. Active May last traded up 1.00, at 94.00 stg. It dominated barley volume, with 63 lots out of a total of 88 lots.
